questions.text:
Let T be a binary search tree with 15 nodes. The minimum and maximum possible heights of T are :
Note: The height of a tree with a single node is 0.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Minimum: a complete tree; 15 nodes fill levels 0-3 (1 + 2 + 4 + 8) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] height 3.
- Maximum: a chain of 15 nodes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] height 14.

Answer: 3 and 14 respectively

questions.text:
The n-bit fixed-point representation of an unsigned real number real X uses f bits for the
fraction part. Let i=n-f. The range of decimal values for X in this representation is
questions.solution:
i integer bits and f fraction bits. The smallest value is 0 (all bits 0). The largest has all bits 1: [latex](2^i-1)+(1-2^{-f})=2^i-2^{-f}[/latex].

Answer: 0 to [latex]2^i-2^{-f}[/latex]

questions.text:
When two 8-bit numbers [latex]A_{7}....A_{0}[/latex] and [latex]B_{7}....B_{0}[/latex] in 2's complement representation (with [latex]A_{0}[/latex]
and [latex]B_{0}[/latex] as the least significant bits ) are added using a ripple-carry Combinational Circuit, the sum bits
obtained are  [latex]S_{7}....S_{0}[/latex] and the carry bits are  [latex]C_{7}....C_{0}[/latex]. An overflow is said to have occurred if
questions.solution:
2's complement overflow happens when both operands have the same sign but the sum has the other sign:
- both negative ([latex]A_7=B_7=1[/latex]) and [latex]S_7=0[/latex], or
- both positive ([latex]A_7=B_7=0[/latex]) and [latex]S_7=1[/latex].

That is [latex]A_7B_7\bar S_7+\bar A_7\bar B_7S_7=1[/latex].

Answer: Option 3

questions.text:
Consider the following context-free grammar over the alphabet [latex]\sum[/latex] = {a,b,c} with S as the start symbol.

S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]abScT|abcT
T[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]bT|b

Which one of the following represents the language generated by the above grammar ?
questions.solution:
Each use of [latex]S\rightarrow abScT[/latex] adds an "ab" on the left and a "cT" on the right; the last step [latex]S\rightarrow abcT[/latex] adds one more pair. T gives [latex]b^m[/latex] with m [latex]\ge[/latex] 1, chosen separately each time.

So: [latex](ab)^n\,cb^{m_1}cb^{m_2}\ldots cb^{m_n}[/latex] with all [latex]m_i\ge1[/latex].

Answer: Option 2
